sections.title: About 1Password
paras: At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

Product Marketing and Enablement connects 1Password’s product strategy to the customer conversations that drive growth. In this Senior Staff individual contributor role, you’ll own the product-to-field motion for Enterprise Password Manager (EPM), Agentic Access—including Developer Tools—and Privileged Access, helping Account Executives (AEs), Sales Engineers (SEs), and Customer Success Managers (CSMs) connect the needs of Information Technology (IT), security, and engineering teams to the right solutions. Through clear technical storytelling, credible sales guidance, and close partnership with Product and Sales, you’ll help 1Password advance its mission to unleash employee productivity without compromising security. Reporting to the Director, Product Marketing and Enablement, this role is remote across the United States and Canada.

sections.title: How we’re using AI today
paras: Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.
This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

ashby:betterup:879cf9aa-e35e-4b3a-8aff-4.summary:
Let's face it, a company whose mission is human transformation better have some fresh thinking about the employer/employee relationship.

We do. We can't cram it all in here, but you'll start noticing it from the first interview.

Even our candidate experience is different. And when you get an offer from us (and accept it), you get way more than a paycheck. You get a personal BetterUp Coach, a development plan, a trained and coached manager, the most amazing team you've ever met (yes, each with their own personal BetterUp Coach), and most importantly, work that matters.

This makes for a remarkably focused and fulfilling work experience. Frankly, it's not for everyone. But for people with fire in their belly, it's a game-changing, career-defining, soul-lifting move.

sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: Our largest customers no longer decide on the demo. They decide on what happens after: whether their HR systems connect, whether provisioning works, whether coaching shows up inside the tools their people already have open, whether our AI behaves the way their risk team needs it to. Forward Deployment is the function that owns that work.

This role takes the accounts nobody has solved. One is an eight-figure decision waiting on a commercial model that doesn't exist yet. On another, the champion left, the last co-creation attempt damaged trust, and we have never been able to see their usage data. On a third, an executive told us the platform is strategic and 2% of the seats have been assigned.

On those accounts there is no charter to execute. You write it. That means deciding what technical success even means here, what we'll commit to, what we'll refuse, and whether a squad belongs on this account at all. Some of these problems are commercial or political rather than technical, and part of the job is recognizing that early, saying so plainly, and not spending engineers on it.

sections.title: What You Own
bullets: Define what technical success means on the hardest accounts in the book. You walk in without a baseline, sometimes without instrumentation and sometimes without trust, and you leave with a written charter, named gates, and a customer who believes the next thing we say.

Commit in writing, in both directions. You say what the squad will build and by when, and you say what has to be true on their side for it to matter. You are equally clear about what we will not build.

Carry the relationship at the altitude where the decision actually sits. You'll work a CIO, a CHRO, a procurement lead, and a security architect in the same week, and you'll be the person our own executives put in front of a customer when the account is in trouble.

Clear the technical gates on the account's next commercial decision. The account executive owns the number. You own the gates sitting on its critical path, and you're measured on gates cleared and on influence the deal team confirms in writing. You carry no quota, and nothing about this role changes that.

Lead a squad of two to three forward deployed engineers, and set the standard the rest of the function calibrates to. You won't manage people. The way you write a charter, run a discovery cadence, and close out an engagement becomes how the other squads do it.

Close every engagement in writing. It graduates into the platform with core engineering's acceptance, it converts to paid or drawdown-funded work, or you kill it. You take those decisions to a monthly graduation board and make the case for the ones worth paving into the platform.

Build the prototypes yourself. Use Claude, Cursor, Replit, and Figma Make to put something real in front of a customer before engineering spends a sprint on it. Adjust prompts, change a flow, and run your own data analysis without filing a ticket.

Own the evidence and the argument it supports. Activation and utilization deltas per account, influence claims the deal team confirms, and the pattern across accounts that tells the product organization what the platform should own and what it should stop building.

sections.title: What You'll Bring
bullets: 7+ years in product management, solutions architecture, or a forward deployed role, including several years owning the technical relationship on enterprise accounts where the contract value ran into seven or eight figures.
A record of turning around an account that was going badly: trust damaged, a previous attempt failed, or a competitor already in the building.

Enterprise deployment experience and the scars that come with it. You've shipped against someone else's HRIS, argued your way through a security questionnaire, waited on procurement, and watched a rollout stall because 40% of the licenses were never assigned.

Enough technical depth to be useful. You don't need to write production code, but you should read an API doc without help, reason about a data pipeline, configure an LLM's context and guardrails yourself, and tell an engineer when an approach won't survive the customer's security review.
Credibility with executives on both sides of the table. You've briefed a customer's leadership team and your own, and you've delivered bad news to both without losing the room.
Experience in B2B2C, where you sell to an enterprise buyer and build for the people that buyer serves. The two want different things and you've had to hold both.
Domain expertise in organizational transformation, human transformation, or talent intelligence is a plus.

sections.title: Skills & Competencies
bullets: Relentless agency. When something isn't working, you own it and fix it instead of naming the team that should have. Humility about what you don't know, and relentlessness about figuring it out anyway.

The discipline to say no. A happy customer asking for one more thing is the hardest no in this job, and so is telling your own leadership that an account they care about isn't a Forward Deployment problem. You can do both without damaging the relationship.

Judgment about what generalizes. You can tell the difference between a custom build worth paving into the platform and one customer's snowflake, and you'll argue for the distinction in front of core engineering.

Executive communication. You can walk into a quarterly business review and tell the story of what you shipped, what it moved, and what you got wrong, to an audience that includes both a CIO and a talent leader.
AI-native fluency. Prototyping with agents is your default operating method, not a novelty you bring out for demos.
Comfort deciding on incomplete information. You listen, synthesize, decide, and move. When you're wrong you correct fast and say so. You don't stall waiting for consensus.

ashby:c1:486afbf3-283c-4368-90ca-095b306.summary:
C1.ai empowers the agentic workforce to put AI to work everywhere. Our platform connects humans and agents to enterprise systems with scoped access, enforced policies, human approval, and a record of every action. With C1.ai , the fastest path to AI adoption at scale is the governed path—giving organizations visibility and control without sacrificing security or slowing innovation. Companies such as Ramp, Zscaler, Qualtrics, and Eli Lilly trust C1.ai to govern workforce access, deploy AI agents, and get work done.

C1.ai is on a mission to secure the agentic workforce, and our brand needs to show up as sharp as our product. We are looking for a Sr. Solutions Engineer to help drive customer adoption and success by delivering technical expertise, guiding customers through evaluations, and architecting secure, scalable identity and access management solutions.

sections.title: What you’ll do:
bullets: Serve as a trusted advisor to prospects and customers on identity governance, authentication, authorization, and access control strategies.
Architect and deliver technical solutions spanning IGA, IAM, CIEM, and PAM, mapping business requirements into scalable identity architectures.
Lead workshops, whiteboard sessions, and demos that showcase the business value of identity automation, access governance, and zero trust.
Design and implement integration strategies across AWS, GCP, and Azure, with a strong understanding of native identity services, policies, and entitlement models.
Nerd out on protocols and standards like SAML, OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SCIM, and FIDO2 — and explain them to both engineers and CISOs.
Build, test, and troubleshoot custom integrations and workflows using APIs, SDKs, and Terraform/automation frameworks.
Stay ahead of industry trends (IGA, CIEM, Just-in-Time access, Zero Trust, identity for machine/non-human accounts) and share thought leadership with internal teams and customers.

sections.title: You would be an excellent candidate if….
bullets: 1-3 years in a technical pre-sales, solutions engineering, or identity architect/engineer role, OR equivalent hands-on experience in IAM/IGA/AI.
Foundational understanding of authentication, authorization, identity services (Okta, Entra AD, LDAP, Google Workspace), and cloud IAM basics.
Practical knowledge of directory services (Okta, Entra ID, LDAP, Google Workspace, on-prem AD).
Hands-on cloud experience with AWS IAM/IAM Identity Center, GCP IAM, and Azure AD/role-based access models, including how to govern them with IGA.
Comfort with GO, APIs, SDKs, JSON/YAML, scripting, and automation, Terraform or similar IaC tools.
Great communication skills and ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Curiosity about identity security and drive to deepen technical knowledge over time.
Willingness to travel for customer meetings, partner events, or industry conferences.

sections.title: Extra Credit if …
bullets: Industry-recognized certifications (CCSP, CISSP, AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.)
You enjoy building new things and presenting new ideas.
You love helping customers understand and solve their access management challenges.

ashby:campus:45019f4e-2f46-4cb0-b664-db9.summary:
Campus is on a mission to accelerate the talent of tomorrow and reimagine what college can (and should) be. The problem is clear: college costs have skyrocketed, but outcomes haven’t. Traditional college hasn’t kept up with the aspirations of today’s students—and they can’t afford to wait.

At Campus, we’ve built a two-year, accredited college where students learn from top professors at universities like Princeton, Stanford, and Howard, in live, online classes. Our students graduate with in-demand business and AI skills—ready to launch their careers or transfer to top four-year universities. Our unique approach is grounded in a pioneering technology platform and a heavily-researched student success model that offers students dedicated advisors and on-demand tutoring and coaching. We were also named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies of 2024 .

sections.title: About Campus
paras: We’re backed by an exceptional investor team that believes deeply in our vision for the future of education, including General Catalyst, Founders Fund, Bloomberg Beta, 8VC, Rethink Education, Sam Altman, Jason Citron, Shaquille O’Neal, and others.
The world has changed. Higher ed needs to catch up, and we’re leading the way - come join us!

sections.title: About the role
paras: As a Senior Product Manager, Core Systems you'll own the strategy, roadmap, and execution of the internal systems that power Campus's business operations, and support the company to scale 10x over the coming years. This includes the roadmap for all financial aid and tuition management, to academic scheduling and program delivery.

We're at an exciting inflection point. As Campus scales, the systems that got us here need to evolve to support what's next. You'll lead the development of scalable, flexible products that streamline operational and revenue workflows, unlock new ways to serve students, and drive meaningful business outcomes.
You'll work closely with our Finance, Business Operations, and Academic Operations teams to tackle challenging problems at the intersection of technology, education, and business operations.

sections.title: You're excited about this opportunity because you will…
bullets: Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for the internal products and systems that power Campus's financial and academic operations, with direct accountability for business outcomes like gross margin and revenue per student.
Build and scale our financial ops platform across financial aid, government funding, tuition, payments, and revenue operations, built for 10x the volume.
Scale our scheduling and program management to support an expanding portfolio of degrees, learning modalities, and student needs while optimizing operational efficiency and resource utilization.
Solve complex problems at the intersection of scale, flexibility, and profitability , balancing the needs of students, internal teams, and the business as Campus grows.

Partner closely with Business Operations, Finance, Engineering, and Design to deeply understand operational workflows, identify opportunities for automation, and translate complex business requirements into intuitive, scalable products.
Drive rigorous, data-informed product decisions , establishing clear success metrics, evaluating tradeoffs, and measuring the impact of your work on operational efficiency, revenue, and gross margin.
Leverage AI, automation, and modern product development tools to simplify complex workflows, improve operational efficiency, and accelerate how we build and deliver products.

sections.title: We're excited about you because…
bullets: 5+ years of product management experience , with a track record of building and scaling complex software products that drive measurable business outcomes.
Demonstrated experience scaling systems through significant growth , whether supporting a 2-3x increase in users, transaction volume, operational complexity, or business scale.
Strong understanding of internal operations and workflow-driven products , such as CRMs, financial platforms, ERP systems, or other business-critical tools.
Exceptional analytical skills and a rigorous approach to measurement , with the ability to connect product decisions to financial and operational outcomes.
Strong business acumen and the ability to make thoughtful tradeoffs , balancing speed, scalability, technical complexity, and long-term business value.
Technical fluency and systems thinking , with the ability to collaborate closely with engineers on complex integrations, data flows, system architecture, and platform scalability.
Strong customer empathy , with an ability to understand the needs of both internal stakeholders and external users and build products that serve them effectively.
Low ego, high EQ, and exceptional cross-functional collaboration skills , with the ability to influence stakeholders across technical and nontechnical teams.

ashby:forus:336f296e-e6a8-4dd1-a651-b3ab.summary:
Forus is building an AI-powered network that connects doctors, pharmacies, payers, and biopharma to accelerate new science to patients.

Our platform automates the complexity between a doctor prescribing a medicine and a patient starting treatment, including insurance coverage, financial assistance, and supply chain navigation. We provide this support free to doctors and patients, helping them get life-changing medicine faster, cheaper, and easier. The resulting network enables biopharma companies to design better research, launch new drugs more effectively, and invest in harder-to-treat conditions.

Forus has exceptional product-market fit and is growing rapidly through organic adoption:

sections.title: About the role
paras: As Manager of the Provider Success Team at Forus, you will own the performance and development of a team of provider success managers, driving provider activation, engagement, expansion and retention. You will turn ambitious goals into clear priorities, build a high-performing team, and shape how Forus earns lasting adoption across its provider network.

You will work directly with your team, provider organizations, and internal partners to resolve escalations, test new approaches to engagement, and improve the systems behind team performance. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will coach individuals, diagnose what is holding results back, and lead changes that make the entire team more effective as Forus grows.

This is a demanding role, with a high level of autonomy and responsibility. You will be expected to "act like an owner" and commit yourself to Forus’ success. If you are low-ego, hungry to learn, and excited about intense, impactful work that drives both company growth and accelerated career progression, we want to hear from you.

sections.title: If you join, you will:
bullets: Lead and develop a team of provider success managers, setting clear expectations and holding a high bar for performance and ownership.
Drive effective engagement and management of relationships with providers and practice staff.
Own monthly and quarterly engagement targets, translating provider activation and retention goals into focused team priorities and measurable results.
Coach individuals to stronger performance, tailoring your approach to their experience, strengths, and development needs.
Hire and develop exceptional teammates, building a team that consistently raises its standards and delivers against ambitious goals.
Drive internal and external escalations to resolution, exercising sound judgment and aligning the right stakeholders around decisive action.
Design and deploy experiments that uncover more effective ways to engage providers, using results to decide what to scale, change, or stop.
Diagnose gaps in processes, materials, and interventions, then lead the improvements and change management needed to deliver better outcomes.

paras: This is a list of ideal qualifications for this position. If you don't meet every single one of them, you should still consider applying! We’re excited to work with people from underrepresented backgrounds, and we encourage people from all backgrounds to apply.
bullets: Experience leading a team of PSMs in a high-growth startup environment, with measurable results against customer engagement, retention, or growth goals.
A track record of exceptional client skills and individual performance before management, with clear ownership of outcomes such as retention or recurring revenue growth.
Demonstrated success hiring and developing high-performing teammates, including coaching underperforming individuals into strong contributors.
Experience identifying why an approach was failing, uncovering the root cause, and leading a team through changes to processes or systems that improved results.
Strong judgment and communication across users, teammates, and senior executives, with the ability to make decisions and organize execution as priorities shift.
A track record of moving quickly, finding shortcuts, and going to unreasonable lengths to deliver on goals.
High NPS with your former teammates, earned through low-ego leadership, tailored coaching, and a commitment to shared outcomes.

sections.title: Working with us
paras:
Forus is based in New York, with our full team working out of a beautiful and spacious office in SoHo.

We run as a high-trust environment with high autonomy, which requires that everyone is fully competent and operates in line with our principles:

Don't wait for the future of infrastructure. Be part of it.

Teleport is the AI Infrastructure Identity Company. We're solving one of the hardest problems in security: giving every human, machine, workload, and AI agent a cryptographically secured identity, improving engineering velocity while maintaining security. We make trusted computing simple. This gives you the freedom, power, and autonomy to build and innovate with confidence.

Remote-first and globally distributed, we work with companies like Nasdaq, DoorDash, and Elastic to secure infrastructure for an AI world.

Teleport is looking for an experienced Product Marketer to produce the messaging and key content to support Teleport’s new product and solution narrative, serve as the source of truth for content that cascades across teams, and drive launches and announcements for Teleport key portfolio solutions that define AI…

sections.title: About Teleport
paras: In this role you’ll help translate complex product capabilities into clear, differentiated positioning that resonates with modern technical teams — including platform teams, infrastructure leaders, DevOps practitioners, cloud security teams, and engineering decision-makers.

You’ll work closely with the Product, Revenue, Solutions Engineering, Corporate Communications, Demand Generation, and Enablement teams to ensure that we meet every audience with the right content. The core content you build will be the foundation that supports our story across programs, campaigns, and sales conversations.

sections.title: Launch Content and GTM Execution
bullets: Own the messaging and content deliverables for new product, feature, and solution launches, from launch brief through the launch content kit.
Turn product and executive narrative direction into core assets: messaging frameworks, positioning documents, product and solution briefs, FAQs, and launch decks.
Run a repeatable launch process that balances rigor and speed, keeping Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Sales aligned from planning through release.
Support announcements and multi-channel activations by providing narrative and source content to Corporate Communications, PR, and Demand Generation.

sections.title: Messaging and Positioning Development
bullets: Work with Product, Solutions Engineers, and other subject matter experts to turn new, industry-leading capabilities into clear, technically credible messaging.
Build consistent, persona-based messaging for platform, DevOps, security, and engineering audiences.
Gather input from customer data, the field, and the community to continuously refine messaging and language as the market and product evolve.

sections.title: Quality and Consistency
bullets: Hold a high bar for writing, clarity, and storytelling across the PMM function.
Maintain a single source of truth for current messaging, so humans and tooling stays accurate and aligned over time.

ashby:halter:f2d7047e-a977-415c-b2d6-02a.summary: At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.

sections.title: About Halter
paras: We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund , Bessemer Venture Partners , BOND, DCVC , Blackbird , Promus Ventures , Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures .
To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram .

sections.title: About the role
paras:
We are searching for a driven and skillful Key Account Manager to work alongside and grow Halter’s enterprise customers. We’re looking for someone with commercial focus, X-factor communication skills, and the ability to drive change and communicate value.

You will be managing a portfolio of large enterprise ranching businesses, from pilot stage through to full-scale integration with Halter technology. You will be responsible for the success and growth of Halter within these accounts. You’ll be an expert at building trusting relationships, identifying opportunities within a ranch system to add value, and enjoying driving the growth of the largest accounts.

You’ll thrive in high-pressure environments, using initiative to make results happen, often against the odds. You might find yourself in a boardroom negotiating a million-dollar contract one day, reporting key KPI’s to a GM the next day, communicating opportunities and driving change with ranch managers by Friday. You’ll masterfully navigate layers within these businesses, adjusting your communication at each level accordingly, to convey the right context and value to all parties. You’ll likely have deep ranch systems knowledge and have a natural ability to drive change on a ranch.

This isn’t a typical role. This is a high-stakes role, playing a critical role in Halter’s growth into the enterprise market segment. Aside from jumping on the Halter roller coaster, you will be making a real-world impact, making ranches more productive and sustainable. You will build relationships across some of the most influential ranching leaders in the United States while working closely with US senior leadership.Up for the challenge? Let’s talk.

Frequent travel is required as part of the position.

sections.title: What your day could look like
bullets: Influencer & Network Management: You won’t stop with your customer. You’ll build relationships with rural professionals, consultants, and other industry influencers who shape opinion and purchasing behavior across your portfolio. You’ll be known and respected in the region as a trusted Halter advisor.

Enterprise Growth Strategy: You’ll collaborate with Business Development and Enterprise Sales to co-create account plans, drive territory expansion, and identify new revenue streams within your customer base. You’ll know your portfolio inside-out and play a key role in shaping how we grow our enterprise presence in-market.

Cross-functional Leadership: You’ll work closely with Halter’s product, support, and sales teams to champion your accounts internally. Whether it’s surfacing product feedback, coordinating training, or aligning on rollout strategy, you’ll be the glue that holds enterprise relationships together and drives results.

Forecasting & Planning: Alongside the Senior Enterprise Sales Manager, you’ll contribute to accurate revenue forecasting and strategic planning. You’ll bring rigor to account performance tracking and identify early signals of both risk and growth.

Scalable Growth Initiatives : You’ll help evolve how we support and grow our largest customers. From refining account management strategies to building scalable playbooks, you’ll be part of the team shaping what great looks like as Halter scales globally.

sections.title: Who are we looking for
bullets: Enterprise experience – You’ve managed large, complex accounts and know how to drive growth over time. You’re comfortable navigating executive rooms, multiple stakeholders, and complex business structures.
Industry fluency – You bring real experience in ranching systems and know what success looks like on a modern enterprise ranch. You’re credible, informed, and customer-first.
Strong commercial instincts – You don’t just nurture relationships; you find value, expand accounts, and deliver results.
Team-first mindset – You collaborate across roles and functions to get the best outcome for the customer and the company.
Autonomy & pace – Y ou’re happy working independently in a fast-changing environment. You solve problems proactively and adjust quickly.
Growth hunger – You’re looking to stretch yourself, take on more, and grow your career alongside a world-class commercial team.
Travel-ready – You’ll be regularly out with customers and regional teams — being in the room, the pasture, or the boardroom when it counts.

Establish clear expectations, operating rhythms, and performance standards for a developing team

ashby:headway:1f473f3b-437d-4781-b0b4-83.summary:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

sections.title: About Payer & Patient Outcomes at Headway
paras: Headway's relationship with payers is evolving from a credentialing and billing partnership to something far more valuable: a network that can prove what it delivers and build products purpose-built for how health plans actually operate. The Payer & Patient Outcomes team owns that transformation — building the products, data infrastructure, and measurement frameworks that let Headway walk into a payer conversation with more than access to sell.

sections.title: About this role
paras: As Enterprise Product Manager, Payer, you'll own the product layer that turns Headway's relationships with its largest payer accounts into differentiated, enterprise-grade product — not one-off features built to placate a single account, but capabilities that create real leverage in contracting and open new ways for payers to engage with Headway. You'll work in lockstep with our Payer BD/Commercial team, translating what actually moves a deal into product requirements, and with Data and Engineering to ship it. This is a build-from-scratch mandate: there's no existing enterprise-product playbook here, and part of the job is creating one.

sections.title: What You'll Own
bullets: Enterprise-tier products built in direct partnership with named strategic payer accounts — the kind of capability that's a genuine reason a payer signs, renews, or expands with Headway
The product-side relationship with Payer BD: translating commercial asks into requirements, and pushing back or reshaping them when a better path exists
A repeatable framework for enterprise payer product work, so builds for one payer become reusable rather than bespoke
Navigating enterprise buying process (procurement, legal, multi-stakeholder sign-off) without importing enterprise pace into how the team builds internally

sections.title: You'd be a great fit if…
bullets: You've operated as a Staff-level PM inside a real enterprise sales motion — you understand what makes a large, slow-moving institutional buyer actually move, and you're comfortable being evaluated by procurement and legal, not just end users
You can hold enterprise rigor and startup urgency at the same time — you don't use "enterprise" as an excuse to slow down
You can generalize a single account's specific ask into something reusable, rather than shipping a one-off every time
You've built trust and gotten cross-functional partners (Engineering, Data, BD) to prioritize your work without having authority over their roadmaps
Healthcare/payer experience is a plus, not a requirement — what matters more is that you've already proven this pace-vs.-rigor tension somewhere else

paras: Most patients open the Headway app about twice a week, almost always for logistics: join a session, message their provider, check an appointment. To them, Headway is where care gets scheduled and billed. It isn't yet a product they want to open.

It should be a best-in-class native experience that uses everything the platform offers, backed by a web portal that removes friction instead of adding it. When a patient has their phone in hand and thinks about their care, Headway should be the first place they go.

This is a product and platform role. Other teams build key features into the app, including AI-powered between-session support, goals, reviews, and rematching. You own the experience they live in: what the app is, how it's organized, how it feels, and whether patients come back.

sections.title: What you'll own:

bullets: The native app as home base. Turn the app from a passive list of appointments into a proactive home that tells patients what to do next. Use the whole app ecosystem. Bring Headway beyond the app itself: widgets, Live Activities, voice assistants, health data, and modern sign-in. Decide when to build directly on platform SDKs and when a third-party integration or platform gets us there faster and works across iOS and Android.
Launch and grow Android. Ship our first Android app so platform is never why a patient leaves or a provider objects. Start with a solid basic app, then set the path toward parity.

A web portal we're proud of. Many patients will stay on the web. Audit the jobs patients do in the logged-in experience, remove the biggest sources of friction, and build a consistent path from web to the app. Decide native vs. web scope feature by feature.

The surface other teams build on. Give partner teams (AI Patient Experience, Search, Profiles, Visitor Growth) a coherent, well-defined place in the app. Set the patterns and interfaces, keep the experience consistent as many teams ship into it, and make the handoffs invisible to patients.
App foundations. Get the app to a level of quality we're proud to promote: reliability, performance, release infrastructure, deep linking, and attribution.

ashby:mercor:38739126-b77b-400b-b1e5-e7b.summary:
Mercor’s mission is to organize human intelligence for the AI economy. We build the infrastructure that enables frontier AI labs and enterprises to train, evaluate, and improve AI on real-world professional work. More than five million experts have joined our network, and we pay out over $5 million daily for their knowledge and expertise.

We built our training and evaluation infrastructure alongside the world’s leading AI labs. Now, we’re bringing those capabilities to enterprises across industries, enabling them to train, evaluate, and improve AI using their own expertise and standards. Our APEX benchmarks measure how AI performs on economically valuable work, while our enterprise evaluations and post-training capabilities turn those insights into measurable improvements across real-world workflows.

Our work sits at the intersection of frontier AI, human expertise, and real-world…

sections.title: About the Team
paras: Frontier models have been trained on most of the public web. The next gains will come from how work actually gets done inside companies: the documents, spreadsheets, code, email, chat, and business systems where real decisions get made, each with its own structure and quirks. That data is private, messy, and inconsistent, and turning it into training data that labs can use and trust is an unsolved problem. The Data Acquisition team works on that problem, turning real-world data into datasets that frontier labs use to train and evaluate their models. Our work spans domains from healthcare and engineering to finance and legal. The same data is valuable at every stage of training, from pre-training to the environments where agents learn to do real work.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: As a Product Manager for Real World Data, you will own how real-world data becomes datasets labs want to buy. You will define what makes this data useful at each stage of training, decide how datasets are shaped, packaged, and delivered, and get high-quality data into labs' hands faster. The role spans product and go-to-market: you will need to understand what is in the data, what labs need, and how to sell it. Working this close to real work, you will see firsthand where frontier models fall short on the tasks that matter most. Real-world data is a new category of product, and what you build will help define it and shape what the next generation of models learns from.

sections.title: In this role, you will:
bullets: Build New Product Lines: Partner with research and environments teams to make real-world data useful for post-training, so agents learn the messy, judgment-heavy work they will face in real workplaces.
Own the Roadmap: Define success in terms of sellable datasets, and use lab feedback, sales outcomes, and unmet demand to decide what the team builds next.

Lead Product Discovery: Define what makes real-world data valuable for pre-training, mid-training, and post-training, and turn that understanding into dataset specifications, quality standards, and ways to measure impact on models.
Define Packaging and Positioning: Turn acquired data into off-the-shelf dataset products, deciding what is sellable, to whom, and in what form.
Set the Quality Bar: Set standards for how datasets are structured, documented, and delivered, and build the visibility to catch problems before delivery and trace each one to its source.
Improve Time to Value: Shorten the path from customer request to accepted delivery by tightening scoping, sampling, and quality review.

sections.title: You might thrive in this role if you:
bullets: Experience: Have 3+ years as a product manager, prior experience in SWE, ML, or DS preferred.
High Ownership: Take full accountability for outcomes, not just outputs.
Independence: Are able to self-direct in ambiguous contexts, creating clarity for others.
Technical Fluency: Are comfortable building scrappy MVPs yourself when needed to validate direction, unblock engineering, or accelerate iteration.
Strategic Vision: Have a strong ability to connect user needs and business context to long-term product direction.
User Obsession and Understanding: Talk to users frequently, know how to effectively conduct user research and customer interviews.
Commercial Instincts: Enjoy the commercial side of product work, and are as effective with lab researchers and account teams as with engineers.
Balance of Metrics & Vision: Are equally comfortable running rigorous experiments and pushing forward visionary bets.

ashby:nabla:64ba6d61-b09d-48cd-bde7-5a2d.summary:
Product development at Nabla is led jointly by Engineering and Product and organized into cross-functional squads. As Senior Product Manager for EHR Integrations , you will own how Nabla lives inside the systems clinicians actually work in.

The EHR is where a clinician’s day already lives, and a large part of the Nabla experience happens inside it. Providers launch Nabla from the chart, and everything Nabla produces (notes, orders, visit diagnoses, codes) has to land in the right place, in the right format, at the right moment. When that fits naturally into how a clinician already works, Nabla becomes something they reach for dozens of times a day. When it doesn’t, even the best AI goes unused. This role owns that part of the workflow, and with it a decisive share of the experience our providers have with Nabla.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Nabla’s EHR integrations across existing and new platforms as we expand.

Design the end-to-end clinical workflow from launching Nabla inside the EHR to exporting notes, orders, and visit diagnoses back into the chart, so it feels seamless to a clinician working under time pressure.
Go onsite with clients to observe how providers navigate their EHR and use Nabla in real encounters, and turn what you see into product decisions and strategic insight.

Build deep technical fluency in each EHR’s capabilities and constraints: APIs, FHIR resources, launch contexts, data models, release and validation cycles, so you can make sound trade-offs alongside your engineers.
Partner with Design to turn hard integration constraints into simple, trustworthy interfaces that clinicians adopt without training.
Collaborate across squads whose capabilities reach clinicians through your integrations, anticipating dependencies and sequencing work accordingly.
Bring Enterprise clients live , working with Customer Success and Technical Implementation to guide health systems through demanding change management, rollout, and adoption.
Define and track the metrics that matter : adoption across encounters, successful export rates, time spent in the chart, integration reliability, and support burden. Let them drive prioritization.

sections.title: Requirements:
bullets: 6–10 years of product management experience , including time spent in healthtech or another regulated, safety-critical industry.
A track record shipping products built on complex integrations (APIs, developer platforms, or third-party systems), including ownership of versioning, documentation, and partner-facing workflows.
Strong systems thinking : you can hold a complex architecture in your head, anticipate dependencies, and make sound technical trade-offs with engineers.
Excellent UX judgment , with a demonstrated ability to turn technical constraints into simple, intuitive workflows for non-technical users.
Deep user empathy and genuine interest in clinician workflows , and the willingness to travel and spend real time onsite with clients.

Exceptional collaboration and communication skills : you are equally comfortable debating a data model with an engineer and walking a health system executive through a rollout plan, and you create alignment across squads and functions.
Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment with incomplete information, competing priorities, and high ownership.
Location: based in our Brooklyn, NY office . This is an in-office-first role (not fully remote), with regular travel to client sites across the US. Full professional fluency in English is required.

sections.title: Nice to have:
bullets: Hands-on experience with Epic or the Epic ecosystem (Vendor Services, Hyperspace, Haiku/Canto), or with Oracle Health (Cerner), athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, or MEDITECH.
Experience with clinical documentation, orders, coding, or revenue cycle workflows.
Prior software engineering experience, or the ability to write scripts and reason about system logs, API schemas, and data models.
Experience guiding Enterprise health systems through change management, go-lives, and multi-site rollouts.
Experience building products powered by ML/AI.
Working proficiency in French is a plus, but not a requirement. Much of our Engineering and Product organization is based in Paris, all work communication happens in English.

sections.title: Life at Nabla
paras: When you join Nabla, you join a team that is driven by excellence, curiousity, and kindness. Together, we’re committed to making clinicians’ lives easier and improving healthcare experiences for everyone. We believe clinicians should be able to focus on what they were trained to do, caring for their patients, and that no patient should feel their visit was rushed.

We work hard and make time to have fun, too. Our #nablabla channel is just as active as #feature-show-off . We support well-being with workday activities at least three times a week; choose from yoga, running, Pilates, or HIIT. We also host regular off-sites, meet up across New York, Paris, San Francisco, and other cities, and keep the chocolate and nuts well stocked.
If this sounds like an environment where you’ll thrive, we look forward to reading your application.

Your point of view influences pricing, packaging, product priorities, and the company's commercial narrative.
You take ownership of some of the most challenging problems with our customers and prospects, and you set the quality bar by doing the work, not by directing it.

You represent Zip with the most senior external stakeholders: CFOs, CPOs, boards, procurement councils, and analysts. Your credibility is critical both in your work, live presentations, and direct conversations.

You build capabilities that outlast any single deal. Frameworks, methodologies, the benchmark foundations, and the value fluency of the go-to-market segment that you engage with are things that extend beyond your immediate presence.

sections.title: You Will
bullets: Set the objectives and approach for Zip's most critical, highest-stakes value engagements.

Own Zip's value methodology end to end: the models, benchmark data foundation, and standards of evidence that every business case at Zip is built on, and the governance that keeps them defensible under Fortune 500 scrutiny.

Represent Zip externally as a thought partner and authority, with customer executives, industry forums, and analysts, bringing back market perspective that anticipates where enterprise procurement value is heading before the business needs it.

Influence company direction with value evidence: feed realized-outcome data and customer economics into product prioritization, pricing and packaging decisions, and go-to-market strategy, and hold those decisions to the standard the evidence supports.

Solve the systemic problems that limit value delivery at scale; where the data foundation is thin, where claims can't be substantiated post-sale, where the field can't reproduce what you do; and build the execution structures that make durable solutions.
Develop value fluency across the wider go-to-market org: coaching reps, raising our internal standards, and creating the conditions for others to grow into greater scope.

Shape how the function uses AI - where AI-assisted modeling genuinely sharpens rigor and speed, where it introduces risk, and what good judgment looks like when a model's output will be defended in front of executives.

bullets: 12+ years of experience with deep domain grounding in procurement, source-to-pay, or enterprise finance transformation.

Demonstrated ownership of company-level or industry-level direction in business value, value engineering, management consulting, or strategic finance - your models and frameworks enabled others to execute without your direct input.

Expertise in enterprise value quantification: you build defensible economic models under genuine uncertainty, state your confidence and assumptions explicitly, and hold up when a CFO's team pressure-tests every line.

Track record of influencing senior executives without authority, internally with company leadership on strategy, pricing, or investment, and externally with CFO- and CPO-level buyers whose decisions carry material commercial consequence.
Ability to navigate systemic, highly ambiguous problems that span multiple teams and functions, anticipate second-order effects, and frame the problem clearly enough that others can act on it.
Sound judgment about AI-assisted analysis: fluent enough to use it for real leverage, rigorous enough to know when its output cannot be defended.
Evidence of multiplying others - coaching senior practitioners, raising a function's quality bar, and building assets and standards the organization keeps using.

Attentive is building an industry-defining Marketing Agent: a unified, autonomous system that understands a brand’s business, decides who to message, when, and with what, and then acts. Brands already trust Attentive with their customer data, and our models know their shoppers deeply. The scope of this role is deliberately broad while the team is built out: the engineer will start by taking direct field cases, shadowing current support, and learning the real demand, then grow into owning complex field cases as repeatable patterns emerge. This role works side by side with IT Service Delivery and partners closely with Service and Controls leadership and with platform teams such as Network, Cloud, and Cybersecurity. The ideal candidate is as passionate about being out in the field as they are about IT — a curious, methodical troubleshooter who takes ownership, communicates clearly with both technical and non-technical audiences, and enjoys learning unfamiliar technology. greenhouse:sentinellabs:7887070003.summary: At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. sections.title: What Are We Looking For?
paras: We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

We are looking for an Executive Product Leader to own Platform and User Experience — bringing together the technical foundation that powers our products and the design experience our customers rely on every day. This is a highly visible, cross-functional leadership role responsible for a major part of our product organization, leading a team of one Senior Director and three Directors, and partnering directly with Engineering, Product, Security Research, and Go-to-Market executives to shape the future of the platform.

This role sits at the center of two disciplines that are often led separately — platform architecture and product design — and requires a leader who can move fluidly between technical strategy (multi-tenancy, RBAC, sovereignty, FedRAMP, API architecture) and design strategy (research, design systems, and AI-driven UX transformation), unifying both into a single coherent product vision.

sections.title: What Will You Do?
bullets: Own the strategy and roadmap for the Singularity Core Platform, including multi-tenancy, RBAC, region deployment, sovereignty, FedRAMP, and API surfaces.
Lead the UX Design team through a transformation toward AI-driven product delivery, emphasizing design judgment and strategic thinking over pixel-level mockups or prototypes.
Lead the UX Research team across the full portfolio, validating product direction against real customer and practitioner feedback.
Guide major investment and build-vs-buy decisions, balancing speed, scalability, and cost.
Direct the evolution of shared platform services — data foundation, APIs, and integrations — that power detection, response, and analytics across the portfolio.
Set the bar for product design and UX, helping security practitioners move from signal to action with speed and clarity.
Drive a consistent design system and research practice across the entire product suite.
Lead and develop a team of 1 Senior Director and 3 Directors, building a scalable, high-performing organization and growing the next generation of product leaders.

Proven experience managing multi-layered organizations (managers and directors, not just individual contributors), with a track record of developing leaders into stronger leaders.
Demonstrated track record setting and executing strategy for both a technical platform and a design/UX function.
Strong executive presence and cross-functional influence, with experience operating as part of an executive team and communicating platform/design strategy to non-technical stakeholders.
Bachelor's degree in a related field (Computer Science, Design, HCI, Engineering, or equivalent experience).

Prior experience building products for security operations, IT operations, DevOps, or other technical, high-stakes practitioner audiences.
Familiarity with the architectural demands of AI-native and data-intensive platforms — real-time analytics, large-scale data pipelines, and the tradeoffs of building a unified data foundation.
A strong point of view on design for complexity — how to make dense, high-stakes workflows (alerts, investigations, response actions) feel clear and fast rather than overwhelming.
Experience in or deep familiarity with FedRAMP, regulated environments, or other high-trust industries.
Advanced degree (MBA, MS, or equivalent).

greenhouse:sigmacomputing:7767898003.summary:
AI only answers correctly when it can trust the data underneath it. This role owns two connected parts of how Sigma shows up in that world: where Sigma's experience lives outside its own product (MCP, a CLI, the Claude and ChatGPT marketplaces, integrations like Slack, Teams, and Glean), and the semantic layer that makes every one of those surfaces trustworthy.

The first mandate is Sigma's AI ecosystem: defining Sigma's approach to MCP, giving external agents structured, governed access to Sigma's data model; owning the CLI, giving developers a fast way to work with Sigma outside the UI; and building Sigma's presence in the Claude and ChatGPT marketplaces, plus integrations for Slack, Teams, Glean, and similar surfaces, so people can reach Sigma's data wherever they already work. This is some of the most visible, fastest-growing surface area in the product.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Define Sigma's approach to MCP, giving external agents and tools structured, governed access to Sigma's data model.
Own the CLI roadmap, giving developers a fast, scriptable way to work with Sigma outside the UI.

Build Sigma's presence in the Claude and ChatGPT marketplaces, along with integrations for Slack, Teams, Glean, and similar surfaces, so people can reach Sigma's data wherever they're already working.
Set the roadmap for Sigma's data modeling strategy, including how semantic views connect across data platforms and how the semantic layer evolves as new AI capabilities emerge.
Partner with engineering and design to ship integration and semantic modeling capabilities that hold up at enterprise scale.

bullets: 5+ years of product management experience in B2B SaaS, data platforms, analytics, or developer-facing products
Familiarity with MCP, APIs, or other machine-to-machine interfaces, and how agents consume structured data
Experience building or launching integrations with platforms like Slack, Microsoft Teams, or enterprise search tools such as Glean
Comfortable defining a CLI or other developer-facing product from the ground up
Strong understanding of data modeling concepts (semantic layers, metrics layers, dimensional modeling) and how they connect across a modern data stack

Some background in BI or analytics is a plus. You should be able to explain why a metric defined once in the semantic layer beats the same metric redefined five different ways across five different tools

Subject to those same considerations, the total compensation package for employees in regular roles may also include other elements, including a bonus and/or equity awards, in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, provided that temporary or intern roles will not be eligible for many of these payments or benefits. sections.title: From the job description
paras: The hardest part of Roboforming is generating a path that will produce the highly accurate part you set out to make. The metal does not want to be formed. It springs back the instant the tool moves past it, and once formed it is packed full of residual stress that wants to pull the part out of spec at any change in environmental conditions. The path we generate is never the part we get, so the real task is finding the path that delivers the part we are after.

Today we find that path by iterating. We form a part, measure the error, and adjust the path to compensate. This works, but it is expensive. Every run cost material, labor, and robot time. To make our manufacturing accessible to broader consumer markets we need to reach the objective part tolerance in fewer trials. We get there by predicting springback before we form.

Traditional solvers cannot get us there. Off-the-shelf FEAs are built for a handful of known loads, not millions of separate small bends. Instead, we need to learn the behavior. This role owns the products that let us do that: machine learning across all the parts we have formed, and GPU based physics simulations where we simulate complex physics.
You will own the models that predicts how the part will spring back and pre-compensates the path, so the very first formed part lands close to the target shape.

smartrecruiters:ifs1:744000161833534.summary:
The Product & Partner Strategy team is seeking a highly skilled and motivated Partner Manager to grow and manage IFS's partner ecosystem across both OEM and ISV partners.

*Candidates MUST be located in the Eastern Time zone.

The Product & Partner Strategy (PPS) team defines and runs IFS's product and solution partner programs across both OEM and ISV partners. The team owns partner recruitment, onboarding, enablement and go-to-market execution, while working closely with internal stakeholders and partners to drive successful partner operations. It also supports Product Managers, Sales and other stakeholders with partner insight, pipeline analysis and commercial support.

sections.title: Job Description
paras: As Partner Manager, you will own the relationship, commercial performance and growth of a portfolio of OEM and ISV partners across the full partner lifecycle. You will be accountable for growing ISV generated revenue and for enabling IFS Sales teams globally to successfully sell OEM partner solutions. Your responsibilities will include:
bullets: Recruit, onboard and offboard OEM and ISV partners.
Own day-to-day partner relationships and act as the main contact between partners and IFS teams.
Maintain partner information and processes on the IFS Marketplace.
Work with Procurement and Finance on partner commercial models, royalties, licensing and payments.
Support Sales in deals involving partner products, including co-sell and go-to-market activity.
Enable partner access to IFS resources such as demos, Demo Showroom and IFS Academy.
Work with Product Managers on partner product use cases with IFS solutions.
Support strategic sales cases requiring non-standard commercial models.

sections.title: In this role you will also deliver against the following key priorities:
bullets: Drive partner recruitment, activation, commercial performance and revenue growth, continually identifying and pursuing new opportunities for growth.
Support strategic initiatives for the partner program and process improvement.
Research competitors, analyse trends and share insights with stakeholders.
Identify opportunities to grow the partner ecosystem and translate strategy into execution.
Improve partner operations through effective collaboration with partners and internal stakeholders.
Create documentation, enablement materials and training content.
Build reports and provide regular and ad-hoc partner performance insights.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: Degree or equivalent qualification in Business Management or a related field.
Experience in partner, channel or alliance management, ideally across OEM and ISV models.
Good understanding of contracts, pricing, licensing and royalty models.
Experience supporting co-sell and joint go-to-market activity.
Ability to align business process, technology and partner strategy.
Tenacious and delivery focused.
Self-driven and able to progress work independently.
Willing to learn, improve and find smarter ways of working.

smartrecruiters:solidigm:744000162365095.summary: This is a commissioned role. The Associate Account Manager is an entry-level sales and account management role within Solidigm’s Global Sales Group (GSG). Solidigm is a leader in advanced NAND technology and SSD solutions serving Hyperscaler, OEM, Neocloud and NAS customers. This role supports account teams in developing customer relationships, coordinating internal execution, tracking account priorities, and contributing to business outcomes across assigned accounts. The ideal candidate is customer-focused, detail-oriented, and motivated to develop commercial, operational, and technical knowledge in the semiconductor and storage industry. Successful candidates will have the opportunity to work directly with some of the world's largest AI infrastructure, cloud, OEM, and storage customers while developing the commercial and technical skills required for future Account Manager roles.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Support account managers and Field Applications Engineers (FAEs) in understanding customer needs, tracking account priorities, and ensuring timely follow-through on customer requests.
Develop foundational knowledge of customer requirements, Solidigm products, sales processes, and market dynamics to support opportunity identification and account growth.
Assist in preparing customer-facing materials, meeting follow-ups, business reviews, forecasts, and internal updates for strategic and tactical account discussions.
Coordinate with Sales, Engineering, Strategic Planning, Global Operations, and other cross-functional stakeholders to support customer execution and business commitments.

sections.title: Operational Responsibilities
bullets: Create, maintain, and update account plans, opportunity trackers, customer action logs, and account documentation.
Maintain accurate opportunity information, meeting notes, customer contacts, and sales activity records in CRM systems.
Support pipeline development, forecast preparation, design win tracking, and revenue reporting in partnership with account leadership.
Partner with internal teams to help resolve customer issues, coordinate deliverables, and ensure effective operational, logistical, and technical support for assigned accounts.

sections.title: Required Skills and Competencies
bullets: Ability to travel up to 50%
Strong interest in sales, customer engagement, semiconductor technology, cloud infrastructure, data centers, or enterprise storage solutions.
Ability to learn technical concepts quickly and communicate product, supply, and business information clearly to internal and customer audiences.
Customer-focused mindset with strong follow-through, responsiveness, and commitment to supporting account teams in a fast-paced environment.
Foundational understanding of business processes such as forecasting, pricing, contracts, supply coordination, customer meetings, or quarterly business reviews.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to summarize information clearly and professionally.
Active listening skills, sound judgment, and the ability to engage professionally with customers and internal stakeholders.
Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work across functions to support issue resolution and customer expectations.

0–2 years of relevant experience in sales, account management, customer success, business operations, or a technology-related role. Will consider a recent College Graduate.
